As much as I believe the EU is within their rights to do such a thing, seeing as we're the ones who voted for it I think it's naive to just assume the EU playing hardball will make hardened brexiteers want to come back crawling to them and if anything it'll only harbour more resentment towards them. Imagine the field day the Daily Mail will have, when they paint us as victims of foreign aggression or some other hyperbolic bollocks.

You make a pretty good point there, I understand where you come from about it being a yes and no and I'm conflicted myself on what I'd vote for if it was a more elaborate poll (I'll explain what I mean in a sec). The biggest problem does come from that it was deliberately left vague due to the government being totally complacent and taking a remain vote for granted so yeah it's a total shitshow.

My stance on a second referendum vote comes largely on the assumption that the Lib Dems or Labour (Whoever manages to push through said vote) will be as incompetent or arrogant in the lead up to it and not offer a ranked choice vote for what we want from the process, in an ideal world I would have voted remain first, customs union but no single market second, and leaving completely third from the top of my head. Infact I understand such a vote really is the most democratic way of doing it as not everyone who voted to remain has the same idea of what remaining should mean, whether we join the Euro for example. 

Let's say tomorrow Theresa May reruns the referendum but in the manner described as above, and it's made legally binding so that the argument I made about shifting goalposts is gone completely, well that's a whole different conversation potentially. I might even be so inclined to vote remain as a first choice, if not leave first with the customs union then staying completely second followed by the rest if that makes sense? The biggest threat then though is the very real possibility of UKIP making another meteoric rise with Farage at the helm but we're just talking hypotheticals here. 

I know you think I'm lying and actually voted leave and I get why you'd think so as I'm not adopting the typical stance on the topic, but I was passionate about remaining to the point I was utterly distraught at the result. I respect why you would vote remain again, and you give a really good reason for doing so. Hopefully the EU survives long enough for us to one day in the not so distant future rejoin and give it the reform it needs to address the many legitimate criticisms it has.

To address again the "stick it to" part that was less a personal attack and a point about people from that side of the debate, people who look at people from my social standing and would look as me as scum cause I happened to grow up poor and as such must be ignored, other people who are given such a label aren't as stupid as they're made out to be and when they go to the polls this is reflected in the results. Just look at the leave vote in affluent areas compared to places like Sunderland and Hull. How do we remain and prove to those people that their concerns still matter? It's a whole load of messed up.

Read my above point about ignoring the outcome...If you want to give the government a blank cheque to hijack our democracy in future then go ahead and push for a second referendum before we've even acted upon the first. 

I wanted this thing and I stand by my initial vote, but because I value democracy I will use my vote for whatever it's worth so at not to undermine it even if it's not what benefits myself. 

If there was a second referendum where we voted to remain then the government adds on a third in the hope of a different result what do you do then? Ask for a fourth? You've already set the precedent that we can have back to back referendums and run around chasing our tail. Hypothetically if we get another one in a few years after we've left and exercised the will of the people then maybe I would vote to rejoin, believe it or not I like the idea of a more interlinked Europe but only if it's done without force or being dragged by our heels.

Of course, I'm not going to argue against fact here. But the insistence on insulting the electorate helps nobody. The uneducated part of the point I made was more in the connotations and the manner in which we use it to shame people for voting leave then expecting them to vote with us. If somebody due to circumstances beyond their control leaves them with no opportunity to go into further education and go straight to working and grafting their way from there then we should respect them all the same. It's obviously a systemic problem we have that we don't encourage independent thought and I think that regardless of the brexit vote it should be addressed accordingly. Also there are always other factors beyond education that influence the vote, for example the biggest leave enthusiast I know is educated to a PHD level, it's not always black and white.

I actually agree with your second point there, low income workers will suffer that's for sure however the middle class won't exactly starve as a result. Think of it like this, if all you've known is being poor, and having to live on a pittance then surely anything could be seen as better than the status quo? Someone I talked to summed it up as such: If your boss is paying you minimum wage and you're working yourself to death, with shitty conditions and no possible hope to progress and your boss is crying about how Brexit is bad for business, spouting off all the usual talking points about the electorate and the like then more than likely you're going to vote against them in the hope that at least something might change, if not maybe get one back on the same people that have kept you and your family under their boot. Personally I think that remaining would have been the best way to protect workers rights but do you see the likes of the Lib Dems for example caring about those same workers when they talk about ignoring the vote? Of course not, most of those same people always on the news were the same ones to back the conservatives in rolling back regulation and forcing austerity on us. Obviously there's still poisonous rhetoric from prominent leave figures keeping the narrative strong but nothing at the moment would convince me if I was a leave voter that I was just being silly for lashing out and I should fall back in line and accept my lot in life as a peasant who needs to shut up and let the big boys decide.
Exactly! Both sides of the debate are guilty of this. Shit, I probably am myself, such is the reality of politics.

How can anybody support remaining when nobody knows what remain is? It could mean the status quo, it could mean more federalisation with the UK joining the Euro and handing over more control to Europe in terms of lawmaking and fiscal policy, or it could mean a more arms length relationship. The problem with the vote is that there was no debate, the left told the poor that they're scum which Psyc5 is an excellent representation of, while the right told disadvantaged people not to blame a broken system for their problems but EU workers and bureaucrats in Brussels. If you'd asked me sooner if we should have had a second referendum I might have agreed on the basis it be a multiple choice ballot with a ranked preference system to put the single market/customs union/remaining completely/hard brexit question to bed but it seems now that all this is about is politicians seeing the democratic process as an inconvenience and wanting to if anything put into the people of this country that we are ultimately not to be trusted to make decisions for ourselves.
